reason: Both answers cover hiQ (CFAA win, contract loss), ToS exposure, data-broker and CCPA exposure, and the C&D-then-suit pattern. A is better calibrated: it says damages are modest while defense costs and loss of the data source are the real hit, and it flags the ProAPIs details as needing verification. It also treats CCPA's publicly-available exemption accurately and adds the vendor-supply risk, copyright, indemnity, and C&D points. B overstates ("zero federal criminal risk", "existential", "most firms fold"). It also includes several shaky or unverifiable specifics (Apollo/Seamless deplatformed, the 6,000 extension IDs, DMCA §1201, the settlement figures, B2B no longer exempt in CA). B's one strong unique point is that company or employee LinkedIn accounts can undermine the Bright Data logged-out defense. That doesn't outweigh its accuracy problems.
